name: Viewport switch (useIsMobile)
summary: The ONE mobile breakpoint (max-width 767.98px) for renders that change shape — the useIsMobile() React hook, a framework-agnostic store, and <aha-viewport-switch> for HTML.
highlights: useIsMobile() React hook and a framework-agnostic store
lead: Mobile in AhaSlides is `(max-width: 767.98px)` — .98 so there is no sub-pixel gap against a 768px rule at fractional device-pixel ratios. Three ways to consume the same decision: React calls useIsMobile() from @ahaslides-product/design/use-is-mobile (react is an optional peer); any framework subscribes through @ahaslides-product/design/viewport (isMobileViewport / subscribeMobileViewport / MOBILE_MEDIA_QUERY); plain HTML wraps both shapes in <aha-viewport-switch> and marks them slot="mobile" / slot="desktop" — exactly one shows, the host reflects a `mobile` attribute, and `viewport-change` fires when the breakpoint is crossed. This is for SHAPE switches only (table → card list, sidebar → drawer); pure styling stays in `@media (max-width: 767.98px)`.
codeNote: useIsMobile() never gates styling — padding, gaps and font sizes belong in the media query. Server renders see desktop (false) and settle on the client.

spec.label: React
spec.value: useIsMobile() from ./use-is-mobile — useSyncExternalStore over the store; SSR = false

spec.label: HTML

spec.label: Event
spec.value: viewport-change { detail: { mobile } } when the breakpoint is crossed

props.name: mobile
props.desc: Set by the element when the viewport is mobile

whenToUse.when: the mobile render is a DIFFERENT shape — a table becomes a card list, a sidebar becomes a drawer
only spacing, sizing or visibility tweaks change — no JS

opinion.note: Never an ad-hoc useMediaQuery('(max-width: 600px)') or window.innerWidth check, and never 768px / 767px in a media query — one breakpoint, 767.98px. Replaces the aha-design plugin's aha-design-shared-components registry entry (SHARED-05).
opinion.dsv3: No DS V3 frame — a behavioural primitive. The breakpoint matches the house responsive rule in aha-design-shared-components §3.

snippets.label: HTML
snippets.note: The native form — a web component in an HTML file renders on open, no build step.

selfCheck.label: exactly one slot rendered; host [mobile] reflects it

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs on the doc page at the 1200px QA window, i.e. the DESKTOP branch: the desktop slot renders, the mobile slot does not, and the host carries no [mobile]. The demo content in each slot is token-styled to prove the slotted shape renders; the 360px branch is verified in a real browser at review.
